# Results — Study 687 (Ladder Bottom) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — a
**ladder bottom** (four consecutive falling candles in a downtrend, then a bullish
reversal candle) marks the end of the downtrend — encoded as two honest cuts: a **loose**
cut (four declining bearish candles, strictly descending closes, then a bullish break)
and a **strict**, literature-closer cut (the loose cut, plus small lower shadows on the
first three rungs, a "warning" upper shadow on the fourth, and a true gap-up on the
fifth). Both are pinned against the **downtrend-matched base rate** — the same long bet
on every bar that already sits in a matching downtrend. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Panel fingerprint
`9693c3ea7807`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLCV, **61 names** (SPY + 60 long-listed US large-caps spanning every major sector), cache-first |
| Window | ~25.0 years per name, ~2001 → 2026-06-30, **383,080** total daily bars |
| Sample fingerprint | SPY: `85f86a841de4` (6,280 rows, 2001-07-10 → 2026-06-30) |
| Detector | loose = 4 declining bearish candles (strictly descending closes) after a downtrend context (close 4 bars back below its level 10 sessions earlier), then a bullish candle closing above the 4th rung's close; strict = loose + small lower shadows on rungs 1-3, a longer "warning" upper shadow on rung 4, and a true gap-up on the 5th candle |
| Execution / costs | ladder confirmed on the close of the 5th candle; entered at the **next open** (one documented lag); long-only; **5 bps** one-way × 2 (round trip); no borrow |
| Statistics | Welch *t* of ladder reversal mean vs the downtrend-matched base-rate mean (the decisive test); one-sample HAC *t* where n permits; a 2,000-draw label-shuffle placebo; **Bonferroni** correction across 4 horizons (critical \|*t*\| ≥ **2.50**); below **8** pooled events, no *t*-stat is computed at all |

No survivorship on the Signal axis in the sense that matters here: this is a
single-pattern event study (not a cross-sectional portfolio), so a fixed,
currently-liquid basket affects which *names* contribute events, not the direction of
the ladder-vs-base-rate comparison.

## The detector — how rare is a real "four down, then up" ladder, really?

| cut | definition | count (pooled, 61 names, 25y) | rate |
|---|---|--:|--:|
| **Loose** | 4 declining bearish candles + downtrend context + bullish break | **2,543** | ~1.67 / ticker-year |
| **Strict** (literature-closer) | + near-low rungs 1-3, warning wick on rung 4, gap-up on rung 5 | **81** | ~0.05 / ticker-year (≈ once per 19 ticker-years) |

Demanding the actual "warning wick + true gap" geometry Nison describes collapses the
candidate pool by more than 30×. As with the desk's other rare candlestick patterns, the
literature's own emphasis on specificity is earned — and it caps what any statistic below
can possibly certify from the strict cut alone.

## Loose cut — four declining candles + downtrend context + a bullish break (n = 2,543)

Bonferroni-corrected critical \|*t*\| for 4 simultaneous horizons: **2.50**.

| horizon | n | ladder mean | win% | base rate | delta (ladder − base) | Welch *t* | placebo *p* | net of costs |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1d  | 2,543 | −3.8 bps | 47.2% | +2.7 bps | **−6.5 bps** | **−1.87** | 0.981 | −13.8 bps |
| 5d  | 2,543 | +46.6 bps | 56.2% | +27.5 bps | **+19.1 bps** | **+2.24** | 0.009 | +36.6 bps |
| 10d | 2,543 | +54.5 bps | 56.2% | +55.5 bps | **−1.0 bps** | **−0.08** | 0.528 | +44.5 bps |
| 20d | 2,543 | +154.7 bps | 59.9% | +120.0 bps | **+34.8 bps** | **+2.12** | 0.011 | +144.7 bps |

**No horizon clears the Bonferroni bar.** Two horizons (5d, 20d) nominally clear a naive
|*t*| ≥ 2 — exactly the kind of "pick a horizon" result the correction exists to catch —
while the 1-day reaction is *negative* and the 10-day reaction is flat. A pattern with a
genuine, persistent edge should not flip sign and go flat between its own reported
horizons.

## Strict cut — the literature-closer ladder bottom (n = 81)

| horizon | n | ladder mean | win% | delta (ladder − base) | Welch *t* | placebo *p* | net of costs |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1d  | 81 | −13.2 bps | 43.2% | **−15.9 bps** | −0.71 | 0.805 | −23.2 bps |
| 5d  | 81 | +107.8 bps | 55.6% | **+80.3 bps** | +1.52 | 0.045 | +97.8 bps |
| 10d | 81 | +129.5 bps | 53.1% | **+74.0 bps** | +1.11 | 0.109 | +119.5 bps |
| 20d | 81 | +339.8 bps | 64.2% | **+219.8 bps** | **+2.30** | 0.006 | +329.8 bps |

The strict cut is directionally more consistent (positive delta at 5/10/20d) and its
best horizon (20d, Welch *t* = 2.30) comes closer to the bar than the loose cut's best
— but it still falls short of the Bonferroni-corrected **2.50**, and the 1-day reaction
is again negative. The 20-day placebo *p* = 0.006 (only 0.6% of random same-size draws
from the downtrend pool beat the observed mean) is the single most suggestive number in
the study — genuinely close, and worth naming honestly — but "close" is not "clears."

### The strict cut's best and worst 20-day outcomes

| ticker | ladder block | 20-day return | context |
|---|---|--:|---|
| MS | 2002-10-02 → 2002-10-08 | **+39.7%** | the October 2002 market bottom |
| KMB | 2020-03-18 → 2020-03-24 | **+21.4%** | the COVID crash bottom |
| BA | 2009-02-26 → 2009-03-04 | **+21.3%** | days before the 2009 GFC market bottom |
| LMT | 2003-01-16 → 2003-01-23 | **−12.3%** | a mid-decline ladder, no reversal followed |
| NKE | 2026-03-10 → 2026-03-16 | **−20.3%** | a mid-decline ladder, no reversal followed |

Some of the biggest winners land right at famous, broad market bottoms (Oct 2002, the
2009 GFC low, the March 2020 COVID low) — the pattern *can* catch a genuine turn. But the
losses are just as large in the other direction, and with only 81 events the mean is
still dominated by a handful of outsized moves either way — exactly why n = 81 needs a
robust test, not a headline anecdote.

## Costs — net of a 5 bps one-way round trip (10 bps total)

| horizon | loose gross | loose net | strict gross | strict net |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1d  | −3.8 bps | −13.8 bps | −13.2 bps | −23.2 bps |
| 5d  | +46.6 bps | +36.6 bps | +107.8 bps | +97.8 bps |
| 10d | +54.5 bps | +44.5 bps | +129.5 bps | +119.5 bps |
| 20d | +154.7 bps | +144.7 bps | +339.8 bps | +329.8 bps |

Where the point estimate is positive, it does survive a 10 bps round trip — costs are
not what kills this pattern. What kills it is that the point estimate is not
statistically certified, and the strict cut fires so rarely (~once per 19 ticker-years)
that there is no meaningful capacity to deploy even if it were.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic panel: 40 names, ~13.9 years each, forced 5-bar ladder blocks (engineered
downtrend + four declining candles + one reversal candle) at a controlled rate with a
TUNABLE planted post-pattern bounce (knob `edge`); no network. The decisive statistic is
the same Welch *t* of ladder mean vs base-rate mean used on the real tape.

| world | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.02** (sd 0.97), \|*t*\| ≥ 2 in **0/20** seeds |
| planted edge = 0.02 (seed 687) | delta **+33.8 bps**, Welch *t* = **+2.85** |
| planted edge = 0.04 (seed 687) | delta **+49.2 bps**, Welch *t* = **+4.02** |

The null is well-calibrated (mean ≈ 0, no seed fires), and a modest planted bounce lights
up cleanly and monotonically. Per the desk's standing rule, **a synthetic control never
backs a Signal stamp** — it exists only to prove the harness can find a real, planted
effect, which it demonstrably can. The honest, unglamorous real-tape result above stands
on its own.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Neither cut clears the Bonferroni-corrected bar (\|*t*\| ≥ 2.50)
  at any of 4 horizons. The loose cut (n = 2,543) is negative at 1d, flat at 10d, and
  only nominally significant (uncorrected) at 5d/20d — the classic "pick a horizon"
  pattern the correction exists to catch. The literature-closer strict cut (n = 81,
  ~once per 19 ticker-years) is directionally more consistent and comes closest (20d,
  Welch *t* = 2.30, placebo *p* = 0.006) — genuinely the study's most interesting number
  — but still falls short, and its own 1-day reaction is negative. No certified reversal
  signal, in either reading.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The literature-closer pattern occurs about **once per 19
  ticker-years** — a curiosity, not a strategy — and even the more frequent loose cut
  (once per ~0.6 ticker-years) fails certification. Where the point estimate is positive
  it survives a 10 bps round trip, so costs are not the binding constraint; the absence
  of statistical certification and of any meaningful event frequency both are.
- **"Beats a downtrend base rate?" — MIXED.** The strict cut points the right way at 3
  of 4 horizons, with an economically large net return (+330 bps at 20d) and a
  suggestive placebo (*p* = 0.006) — this is not a "backwards" result like a bearish
  pattern that loses money short. But the best number (*t* = 2.30) falls short of the
  Bonferroni bar, the 1-day reaction is negative, and the sample (n = 81) is thin enough
  that three of its five best/worst events could plausibly be describing famous *market*
  bottoms (2002, 2009, 2020) rather than the ladder shape itself. Not busted, not
  confirmed — genuinely mixed, and too rare to resolve further on this basket.
